items.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: They did some records where they used their voices singing together, with the instruments of the orchestra, and it was vocalese all the way, no lyrics, and we said hey that’s great.

ctx.x: So I said no, no, no deal. We went to the bar and libations, and Vete [Bob Anderson] said, “ah come on, she’s good.” She’ll — okay. She sang “Happiness is Just a Thing Called Joe.” And I happened to have loved that song because hearing Frances Wayne sing it with Woody Herman’s band, a Neal Hefti arrangement. I said God, that’s great. Okay. And she sang that. The club owner was there that night, and he came up to us and said, “you guys need a singer for Friday and Saturday.” Okay.

And that’s how we started working together. But I was just the girl singer. I mean we didn’t do things together in the beginning. I was just singing ballads and uptempos and do a few tunes every set. And the group was quite a good group. And then eventually as we went along, suddenly we heard, let’s see Buddy Stewart and Dave Lambert with Gene Krupa. We had heard it around that time. They did some records where they used their voices singing together, with the instruments of the orchestra, and it was vocalese all…

composer. So we said let’s do something similar to that, in our own way. So he started writing some little arrangements for us, which were generally the tune first, with the lyrics, and then it went into a vocalese part. And we had quite a few in our repertoire, and that’s actually when Charlie Ventura heard us, at a Dave Garroway concert.
